summary.text: Cory Booker is the incumbent Democratic U.S. Senator from New Jersey, in office since October 2013. A Stanford, Oxford and Yale Law graduate, he started a legal-services nonprofit in Newark, served on the Newark City Council (1998-2002) and as Mayor of Newark (2006-2013), and ran for the 2020 Democratic presidential nomination. He ran unopposed in the 2026 Democratic primary and chairs the Senate Democrats' Strategic Communications Committee.

paragraphs.text: Booker was born in Washington, D.C., in 1969 and grew up in northern New Jersey. At Stanford University he played varsity football and earned a bachelor's degree in political science in 1991 and a master's in sociology in 1992.
As a Rhodes Scholar he earned a graduate degree in history at the University of Oxford in 1994, and he received a J.D. from Yale Law School in 1997.

After law school Booker moved to Newark and, according to his Senate biography, started a nonprofit providing legal services to low-income families. He was elected to the Newark City Council at 29 and served from 1998 to 2002, and he was Mayor of Newark from 2006 to 2013.

Booker won a special election to the U.S. Senate in October 2013 and was re-elected to a full term in November 2014 and again in 2020. His Senate biography cites his work on the First Step Act, a criminal justice law enacted in December 2018.
He announced a campaign for the 2020 Democratic presidential nomination on February 1, 2019, and suspended it on January 13, 2020.

He serves on the Senate Judiciary, Foreign Relations, Agriculture, Nutrition, and Forestry, and Small Business committees. Senate Democrats elected him chairman of their Strategic Communications Committee without opposition on December 3, 2024.

On March 31, 2025, Booker began a Senate floor speech that lasted 25 hours and five minutes, the longest in Senate history. He advanced from the June 2, 2026, Democratic primary as the only candidate on the ballot, and according to his Senate biography he lives in Newark's Central Ward.
